What it would do differently

The leads the player wrote, each with where it happened and what would settle it. An ask is a link into the replay above.

  1. Where is the down staircase of this level, and is the western third enterable at all?

    The generator puts it on a square with exactly three adjacent walls, uniformly.

    What would settle it: a run that maps the level from the western end — that is, one that goes up to the town and comes down and then walks west along the southern rows, which is the only route I could not find.

  2. Does a level have more than one down staircase?

    My notes said one; the source says alloc_stairs(c, FEAT_MORE, 1, ...) — one. This level had three up staircases, so the generator does allocate several of those, and the question is whether the down one is also plural.

    What would settle it: read gen-cave.c around the alloc_stairs calls for FEAT_LESS and FEAT_MORE and say what each asks for.

  3. Is the down staircase always at a dead end, and are dead ends common enough to be searched for?

    alloc_stairs tries three adjacent walls first and then falls back to two, one and zero.

    What would settle it: count the dead ends on a level, and the number of them divided into the number of squares, which gives the chance that a random walk finds it.

  4. Does a depth-1 chest ever have anything in it?

    Four said no on this level and one said no in the first life.

    What would settle it: read the chest placement code (place_chest in gen-stairs.c or cave.c) and see whether a depth-1 chest is generated with contents.

  5. What is the real relationship between the M map and the level?

    My three lives disagreed and the source says it scales the whole level. The one thing I could not do is read the M map's scale exactly: 78 columns for 198 squares is 2.54 squares a column, so a single remembered staircase could be drawn over by a neighbouring tile.

    What would settle it: a run that finds a > in the western third and checks whether the M map shows it.

  6. Can a level-1 druid be made to level at all?

    The formula says no.

    What would settle it: a run that kills twenty depth-1 small kobolds and counts the experience, which is the only way to be sure that the quarter-unit estimate is right and not an artefact of the integer division.

- Giant black ant: 11 hp, AC 24, 1d4 bite, exp 8 (monster.txt) - and it is ASLEEP ('unhurt, asleep'). One flask of oil (9-36 damage) should kill it, and 8 exp takes me from 13 to 21, past CL2 (14) most of the way to CL3 (25). Its AC 24 against my to-hit 19 means the whip is hopeless, so oil it is. - THROW MISSED the sleeping ant at distance 2 (ask 201: 'The giant black ant is targeted... The Flask of oil breaks' with NO damage line, and ask 205 confirms the ant is still 'unhurt, asleep'). Source reading (vendor/angband/src/player-attack.c): make_ranged_throw() applies the OF_EXPLODE x3 damage ONLY if test_hit() passed - a miss breaks the flask on the floor and does nothing. The hit chance is chance_of_missile_hit_base() minus distance, against the monster's AC. The ant's AC 24 (monster.txt) is brutal: hit_chance() needs to_hit >= ac*2/3 = 16 to have any chance above the flat 12% always-hit, so at range you are mostly rolling the 12%. (ask 205)

Lesser Charms is a nature book with 6 spells. The CL2 spell Remove Hunger is worth little (food is not a time pressure here - digestion is 1 unit per 100 turns, per my inherited note), so Stinking Cloud at CL3 is the prize, if the game lets me study a spell above my level. - Studied Remove Hunger at ask 217: 'You have learned the verse of Remove Hunger.' and NXT stayed at 7 - so STUDYING a spell costs no experience; the exp field in class.txt (Detect Life 2, Fox Form 10, Remove Hunger 2) is the FIRST CAST cost, not the learning cost. Also confirmed the game REFUSES to study a spell above your class level: at CL2 pressing 'd' (Stinking Cloud, CL3) in the Study prompt did nothing and left the prompt up. So a druid must reach CL3 before Stinking Cloud can be learned, and 'Study (1)' means one verse per character level. (ask 217)
- KEY ERROR OF MINE, worth recording so no next run repeats it: after pressing 'l' (look) the look mode STAYS ACTIVE and swallows the next command's first key. At asks 221-225 I sent 'l', then 'va\'', then 'va1' and nothing happened - the look descriptions ('You are on an open floor', 'You see a yellow mushroom patch') kept printing and no turn passed, because the keys were being read as look-mode cursor moves, not as 'throw'. The tell is that the turn counter did not move and the message line showed a LOOK description. Press '\e' to leave look mode before any other command. With look mode properly closed, 'va\'' works exactly as advertised: 'The yellow mushroom patch is targeted' / 'Your Flask of oil hits the yellow mushroom patch' / 'The yellow mushroom patch is destroyed' (2 exp, NXT 7 -> 5). The yellow patch was the reason the west corridor was lethal - adjacent to it you get TERRIFIED. (ask 229)
- TWO OIL THROWS AT THE SMALL KOBOLD BOTH MISSED (asks 235, 236) and it hit me for 2 (HP 20/22). Its AC 24 against my throwing skill is the problem, not the damage: hit_chance() in player-attack.c needs to_hit >= ac*2/3 = 16 to have more than the flat 12% always-hit, and a throwing flask at range 1-2 lands around 30-60. LESSON: the depth-1 monsters that are worth killing with oil are the LOW-AC ones (white worm mass AC 1, grey mould AC 1, yellow patch AC 1, mouse AC 4, centipede AC 12-14). A small kobold (AC 24) and a giant black ant (AC 24) are oil targets only from 1 tile away. The giant black ant died from range 1 with one flask; the same flask at range 2 missed. (ask 237)
- Detect Life at ask 238 said 'You sense life!' and set MFLAG_MARK+MFLAG_SHOW on every living, non-camouflaged monster within 22 rows x 40 columns (vendor/angband/src/effect-handler-general.c detect_monsters). The map then shows them even outside the light radius - but the text dump I get does not show the blinking MARK highlight, only the SHOW part, so the detection is of limited use to me as a player: I see 'You sense life!' and then the map may or may not have gained glyphs outside my light. A plain-text player cannot use Detect Life the way the manual implies. Small kobold killed at ask 240 (2 oil flasks, both at range 1), NXT 5 -> 3, so 3 more units for CL3 and Stinking Cloud. (ask 240)
- GLYPH TABLE now decoded from vendor/angband/lib/gamedata/terrain.txt (each 'graphics:<char>:<colour>' line): space=unknown grid, .=open floor, +=closed door, '=open door (u=broken), <=UP staircase, >=DOWN staircase, 1-8=stores, #=secret door or granite/permanent wall or lava, :=pile of rubble, %=MAGMA VEIN or QUARTZ VEIN (a solid wall - the colour tells them apart, a text dump cannot), *=vein with treasure. So the corridor I am in is a vein-walled passage: the '%' above and below me are walls, not floor, and the fact that they are drawn '%' and not '#' only tells me they are rock veins. There is no '>' anywhere on the map of depth 2 yet. (ask 243)
- THE '[' COMMAND IS THE BEST ONE-ASK SCAN IN THE GAME: it prints 'You can see N monsters:' with the glyph, the COUNT, the name and the exact relative position of each - e.g. 'c   1 giant yellow centipede    2 S 0 W' (ask 245). That is a monster-list panel with the relative offset, so a player who cannot use the map can still know exactly what is around and how far. It even offers 'Press x to turn ON sort by exp'. Combined with 'l' (look) in a direction, which snaps the cursor to the next interesting square and reports 'N N, E W', I can reconstruct the local geometry without ever reading a pixel of the map. (ask 245)
- QUAFF SEQUENCE that works in one ask: 'q' then 'd' (the quaff prompt prints 'Quaff which potion? (Inven: d-d)' and the pack letter selects it). 'qdq' does NOT work - the third key is read as the Drop option of the item command menu, and the game then asks 'Drop which item?'. Also 'q d ' opens the item-command menu instead of the quaff prompt; pressing 'q' there quaffs. So: q, d. (ask 253)
- M (whole-level map) on depth 2 at ask 260 shows ONLY the region I have seen - a blob about 18 map columns wide around me - drawn at a scale that differs from the main map, so I still cannot read absolute level coordinates out of it. The main map's window also scrolls, so my absolute position is not recoverable from a single screen either. PRACTICAL CONCLUSION for the report: the level is 198x66 (constants.txt dungeon-wid/dungeon-hgt) and the map window is 36x22, so a level is about five screens wide and three tall; locating a staircase by reading maps is hopeless for a text player, and the only tool that works is the game's own pathfinder (lxg) plus scanning every map for a '>' glyph. (ask 260)
- Found and picked up an UNIDENTIFIED scroll on depth 2 (ask 273), title 'imusto que', dropped by a small kobold at 100 feet. Deep Descent has level:10 and alloc:20:1 to 100 in object.txt, so at CL2 it is exactly this: a scroll with a random title that only identifies at level 10. Reading it at CL2 is what the knowledge in NOTES.md says to do (unknown consumables at CL1-3 are worth trying; the first use pays a little experience). If it is Deep Descent it drops me 5 levels below my deepest level reached - depth 2 + 5 = depth 7. Worst plausible case is Summon Monster (cost:0, alloc:10) or Darkness or Blessing. Word of Recall is the way home if depth 7 goes badly (read in the dungeon = town, 15-34 turns). (ask 274)
- The unidentified scroll on depth 2 turned out to be a Scroll of LIGHT, not Deep Descent: 'You are surrounded by a white light' then 'You have no more Scrolls of Light (g)'. So it identified at first use and cost no experience (NXT stayed at 2) - Light's exp field in class.txt/object.txt is small. Harmless, and now known. What I can say about the DROP: it was dropped by a small kobold at 100 feet (level 2), so a depth-2 kobold carried a Scroll of Light - the monster drop table is a real source of consumables, and killing a monster is a way to GET a scroll rather than hoping to find one on the floor. (ask 277)
- DECISIVE TEST of the manual's 'l>g' recipe: in look mode press '>' and the cursor jumps to the nearest KNOWN down staircase (vendor/angband/src/ui-target.c, path_nearest_known with square_isdownstairs). On depth 2 at ask 284 I tried it and there is NO known down staircase anywhere in the level I have explored - so the recipe cannot help until a '>' glyph has actually been seen. That is the real reason 'no run has ever found a down staircase': not that the staircases are rare, but that the game's own jump only works on a staircase you already know about. The way to know about one is to LOOK at the glyph (the 'l' command named it for me on depth 1: 'You see a down staircase, 1 S, 1 W'), so a player who reads every glyph on every map has a chance and a player who trusts the frontier logic does not. (ask 284)
- SOURCE ANSWER to the repo's standing question 'is the down staircase findable at all': NO SPATIAL RULE EXISTS. gen-cave.c:1583 allocates exactly ONE down staircase per level (alloc_stairs(c, FEAT_MORE, 1, 0, ...)), gen-util.c:620 places it on a square with exactly 3 adjacent walls, and cave_find_get_grid() (gen-util.c:202) picks that square by random choice over the WHOLE level (state[] holds every square in the level and the next one is drawn with randint0). So the down staircase is uniform over the level's floor squares - there is no 'it is near the up staircase' or 'it is in the biggest room' heuristic to exploit. The level is 198x66 with up to 50 rooms (dungeon_profile.txt 'classic' params:11:50:200:2), and the map window is 36x22, so a level is about five screens wide and three tall. Finding one by walking is a matter of covering thousands of squares; the previous run's 148 asks and my 140 have not come close. The reliable routes are a Deep Descent scroll or a Magic Mapping scroll, and neither was available to me. (ask 289)
- ENDGAME NOTE for the report: with one down staircase placed uniformly at random on a 198x66 level and a 36x22 map window, and no detection tool in the pack (no Magic Mapping, no Find Stairs spell for a Druid), the probability of finding it by walking in the remaining budget is small. I spent my last asks walking the corridor south of the big room, which is the region the frontier logic kept pointing at, and scanning every map I have drawn for a '>' glyph with a script over the screen files - the only real one was the depth-1 staircase at asks 160-162. Depth 2's down staircase was never seen. (ask 300)
- LEVEL 3 at ask 306 (from the sleeping giant green frog: 9 hp, AC 9, exp 6, killed with one flask of oil at range 1 - a much better oil target than anything else on this level). HP 22/26, SP 3/5, 'Study (1)' is back, and NXT 25 means CL4 is 25 experience units away. Grip, Farmer Maggot's Dog (the DL2 unique: 25 hp, AC 36, 1d4, speed 120 = +10 speed, exp 30) is 2 tiles south of me and AWAKE, so I am not going to fight it - but its 30 experience units are what CL4 wants. (ask 306)
- STINKING CLOUD SOURCE READING (effect-handler-attack.c:594, effect_handler_BALL): the flags are PROJECT_THRU|PROJECT_STOP|PROJECT_GRID|PROJECT_ITEM|PROJECT_KILL and PROJECT_PLAY is NOT among them, and project() only affects the player when PROJECT_PLAY is set (project.c:519 and :996). So a druid's Stinking Cloud CANNOT hit the caster, even when the ball is centred on a monster 2 tiles away. That is a big deal for a 26 HP druid: the radius-2 poison ball is a safe weapon at point blank range. Damage = PLAYER_LEVEL/2 + 10 = 11 poison at CL3, halved with distance from the centre. (ask 310)
- GRIP (Fang and Grip, the DL2 uniques) against a CL3 druid, measured: 25 hp, AC 36, bite 1d4, speed 120, exp 30. Stinking Cloud hit it ('yelps in pain', health bar [******----], about 55%) and cost me 12 experience on the first cast. A flask of oil at point blank MISSED - AC 36 means the throw hit chance is hopeless, the same lesson as the small kobold and the giant black ant but worse. It bit me for 5 and chased me north, so my HP is 11/26 and I have 1 SP of the 2 a cast needs. The spell is the only weapon that can hurt it, and I cannot pay for it while it is on me. (ask 318)
- THE FIGHT WITH GRIP, measured: it bites for 2-4 a turn against my AC 12 (much less than its 1d4 suggests, because AC 12 cuts most of the small dice), and it WAKES me if I try to rest - but a counted rest ('R' then a number) runs the full count anyway, taking the hits as they come. Spell points are the bottleneck, not hit points: 4 turns of rest bought no SP at all, so ~10+ turns of rest are needed for 1 SP. Stinking Cloud is the only weapon that can hurt it (AC 36 - a flask of oil at point blank MISSED, and so did one against the kobold at AC 24). Two casts of 11 poison would finish its remaining ~17 hp. (ask 323)
- ESCAPE LADDER in practice, measured: against Grip (AC 36, 25 hp, +10 speed, biting me for 2-4 a turn in a one-wide corridor) I could not fight it - a flask of oil at point blank missed, my whip has a 12 percent chance against AC 36, and the spell that CAN hurt it costs 2 SP while I had 1. THE SPELL POINT ECONOMY IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, and the source explains it: player-util.c:487 player_regen_mana() computes sp_gain = msp * PY_REGEN_NORMAL + PY_REGEN_MNBASE, with PY_REGEN_NORMAL = 197 and PY_REGEN_MNBASE = 524, both in 65536ths (player-util.h:27,31), and doubled while resting. For msp = 5 that is about 0.023 SP per turn, so ONE spell point costs roughly 22 turns of rest, and a Stinking Cloud needs two. Resting beside Grip for 90 turns is not a plan. So the Phase Door scroll is not a luxury - with a 2 SP weapon and no melee that reaches, the scroll IS the weapon. (ask 327)
- PHASE DOOR ESCAPE WORKED AND COST NOTHING: 'You have 2 Scrolls of Phase Door (e)' and the cursor moved from level (44,14) to level (52,8) - 10 grids, exactly as the scroll says ('When read, it teleports you randomly 10 grids'), and the monster list then said 'You can see no monsters', so Grip was left behind with no cost and no delay that I could see. The scroll is BUG-free for this job: 1 ask to open the pack, 1 to select the scroll, 1 to read it, and a 10-grid teleport. The lesson for any character with no working melee: the Phase Door scroll, not the spellbook, is the weapon. What I still cannot do is kill Grip - 25 hp at AC 36 with 1d4 and +10 speed, and a spell I cannot pay for. (ask 333)
- GREY MOULD KILLED at range 1 with one flask (2 hp, AC 1 - a certain hit at that range, 3 experience). The mould was the one monster on this level that could actually reach and hurt me: it is MOBILE (no NEVER_MOVE flag, unlike the mushroom patches) and it does 2 x SPORE:HURT:1d4, so up to 8 damage a turn against my AC 12. Two bites of it brought me from 25 to 22. It bit me while I was trying to read a scroll, which is worth knowing: a spell or scroll takes a turn, and the turn the spell resolves on is a turn the monster also acts. (ask 348)
- THE BEST SCANNING TOOL IN THE GAME, found by accident: cast Detect Life and then press '['. The detection sets MFLAG_SHOW on every living monster within 22 rows x 40 columns (effect-handler-general.c detect_monsters), and the '[' list then shows a SECOND section headed 'You are aware of N monsters:' with the glyph, count, name, sleep state and the exact relative position of each - including monsters that are out of sight and were not in the 'You can see' list. At ask 361 that gave me: Grip 5 S 3 W, a green worm mass (asleep) 17 S 3 W, and TWO giant yellow centipedes (2 asleep) - all invisible to the eye and all on the map. This is worth more than the spell's own effect: the spell is the only thing in the game that gives a player a monster list over a 22x40 area, and the manual never says so. (ask 361)
- SPELL POINT ECONOMY MEASURED, and it is the single most important number for a druid: with msp = 5 at CL3, player_regen_mana() gives sp_gain = msp * PY_REGEN_NORMAL + PY_REGEN_MNBASE = 5*197 + 524 = 1509 in 65536ths = 0.023 spell points per turn, doubled to about 0.046 while resting. So ONE spell point costs roughly 22 turns of RESTING and 43 turns of not resting, and a Stinking Cloud needs two of them. I rested 20 turns and gained nothing at all (SP stayed 1/5, HP went to 26/26). For a class whose only good spell costs 2 SP, the spell book is nearly decorative until the character can afford to sit still for a minute of game time. (ask 363)
- GRIP KILLED at ask 367: 'Grip, Farmer Maggot's Dog, dies. Welcome to level 4.' Three flasks of oil in total against it, two of them hitting, at ranges 1 and 2. That is the whole recipe for a DL2 unique as a CL3 druid: never melee it (my whip is 1d3+1 at to-hit 19 against its AC 36 - a 12 percent chance), never rely on the spell (2 spell points that take 43 turns of rest to earn), and just throw oil from range until one lands. It gave 30 experience and took me from NXT 12 to level 4. Final state: depth 2, CL4, 26/26 HP, 1/5 SP, 24 flasks of oil, 3 Cure Light Wounds, 1 Scroll of Word of Recall, AC 12, and no down staircase found on depth 2. (ask 367)
- CL4, HP 26/33, SP 1/7, NXT 28 (so CL5 needs 28 more). Studied Fox Form at CL4: the spell list at CL4 is Detect Life (1 sp), Fox Form (2 sp), Remove Hunger (2 sp), Stinking Cloud (2 sp, 'dam 12, rad 2' now that I know it - it was 11 at CL3, so the poison scales with level as class.txt says: PLAYER_LEVEL/2 + 10). Confuse Monster is CL5 and Slow Monster CL6, so neither is available yet. Fox Form (shape.txt: combat:-3:-3:3 = -3 to-hit, -3 to-dam, +3 AC; STR[-3], BLOWS[1], MOVES[1], FREE_ACT, FEATHER) is the druid's only intrinsic escape, and I had just been chased by a +10 speed dog that I could only fight with oil. Its costs are real: -3 to my already weak whip, -3 STR, 10 experience on the first cast, and no items while shaped (no quaffing a Cure Light Wounds while a fox). (ask 370)
- Testing the Word of Recall, which no run in this repo has ever used: read in the dungeon it sets a timer (player->word_recall = randint0(20) + 15 turns, effect-handler-general.c:1141) and when it expires it takes you to town ('You feel yourself yanked upwards!', game-world.c:709-727). The timer is NOT interrupted by damage - it is a plain countdown - so it is only a safe way home when nothing is chasing you, which is exactly why c15 ESC-04 does not count it as an escape. (ask 374)
- WORD OF RECALL VERIFIED, and it is better than the manual says. Read in the dungeon: 'The air about you becomes charged...', the status line then shows 'Recall' between Light and Fed, and after the timer expires 'You feel yourself yanked upwards!' and the depth becomes 0 (town). The timer ran about 26 turns (turn 10252 to 10501) and was NOT interrupted by anything - I simply rested through it. Crucially, arriving in town HEALED ME TO FULL (28/33 -> 33/33) and gave back 2 spell points, because town has no monsters and the character regenerates there. So the scroll is not an escape (c15 ESC-04 is right - the delay is too long to survive a chase) but it IS a free full heal and a free trip to the shops when nothing is chasing you. (ask 381)
- TOWN NAVIGATION on seed 23, from the town's own map (the town fits the screen, 66x22 in one panel): the stores are at town screen row 11 col 50 (7 Black Market), row 11 col 63 (5 Alchemist), row 11 col 23 (4 Bookseller), row 12 col 28 (6 Magic), row 12 col 36 (2 Armoury), row 12 col 43 (1 General), row 12 col 55 (8 Home), row 17 col 44 (3 Weaponsmith); the down staircase is at row 4 col 32 where you arrive. The store tiles are NOT walkable - the walkable square is the one orthogonally adjacent to the digit, and the path I computed to the Black Market from the arrival point was 6 south then 10 east. (ask 382)
- BLACK MARKET (store 7) STOCK ON SEED 23, the shop the previous run never visited: Lo-Hak the Awful (Half-Troll). Wand of Stun Monster (5 charges) 1875, Staff of Curing (7 charges) 2025, Lantern of Brightness (7500 turns) 3150, 11 Robes [2,+0] 42, 3 Sets of Gauntlets [3,+0] 72, Trident of Slay Animal (1d10) (+5,+7) 4902, 10 Arrows of Wounding (1d4) (+9,+13) 309. NO Deep Descent and NO Magic Mapping. The reason is in the source: store_create_random() in store.c picks the Black Market's stock as a random object of level player->max_depth + 5 to + 20 (so level 7 to 22 for me at depth 2), and the price is 150 percent of the true value (store.c:617) - the Deep Descent's base cost is 250, so it would have been about 375 and hopeless on 26 gold anyway. The cheapest useful thing there is a robe of +2 AC for 42 gold. (ask 384)
- ALCHEMIST STOCK ON SEED 23, LATER IN THE DAY - and it answers the previous run's open question: 'Magic Mapping 65 g did not help' and 'the Alchemist did not stock one this seed'. The Alchemist RESTOCKS EVERY DAY and rolls a fresh stock from its normal list, and the shopkeeper itself changes (Mauser the Chemist / Wizzle the Chaotic / Ga-nat the Greedy / Vella the Slender). At ask 399, under Vella the Slender, the stock was: 40 Potions of Cure Light Wounds 20, Potion of Cure Serious Wounds 70, 5 Potions of Cure Critical Wounds 200, Potion of Restore Life Levels 400, 2 Potions of Berserk Strength 80, 40 Scrolls of Phase Door 15, 3 Scrolls of Magic Mapping 65, 40 Scrolls of Remove Curse 100, 40 Scrolls of Word of Recall 125, 3 Scrolls of Recharging 200, 9 Scrolls of Holy Chant 40. SO MAGIC MAPPING IS FOR SALE - three of them - for 65 gold. I could not buy it: a street urchin stole 8 of my 26 gold in town and I was down to 18. The lesson for the next run is sharp: BUY THE MAGIC MAPPING SCROLL FIRST, in the Alchemist, on whichever day it is in stock, and go back to town for it - a level of gold spent here saves 200 asks of blind exploration. The stock rolls when the game day changes (store.c store_maint is called once per daycount, and the shopkeeper shuffles on a 1-in-z_info->store_shuffle chance per day). (ask 399)
- CARRIED ON from minimaxflash-1.2 at ask 400, turn 10888, replay identical=true. Files I actually opened for THIS session: CONTINUEGAME.txt (all), AGENTS.md, docs/BRIEF.md, manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md (all), knowledge/NOTES.md (all), knowledge/LEARNED.md (all), knowledge/MANUAL-GAPS.md (all), plus my own write-ups runs/minimaxflash-1/REPORT.md and runs/minimaxflash-1.2/REPORT.md and inherited notebooks for those two lives. NOT read: any other run's decisions, report, notebook, or replay; PLAN.md. (ask 400)
- At ask 412 the same street urchin stole 15 more gold while walking west: AU 18 to 3, while the run went from town (70,15) to (60,15). This repeats ask 394's 8-gold theft and confirms town thieves can strip nearly all carried gold during a long movement. The countermeasure is not available because selling pays zero, so the practical rule is: do not carry gold while roaming; spend it before walking far, and return to a shop tile when a thief is nearby. (ask 412)
- At ask 427 the game's look-mode jump worked in TOWN: 'l>' said 'You recall a down staircase, 5 N, 9 E.' and the next 'g' began walking toward it. After manual navigation I reached the town down staircase at ask 436 (cursor 40,4, status 'Down staircase'). This confirms the inherited note's l>g recipe is useful even in town, where the staircase is already known; the earlier inherited report had focused on dungeon stairs. Town thieves also cost 15 gold during this walk (18 to 3 at ask 412), and repeated dog/rogue attacks took HP from 32 to 16 by ask 435. (ask 436)
- THREE NEW MECHANICS, all measured this life: (1) The '>' jump to a KNOWN down staircase works in LOOK mode ('l>') as well as in targeting mode ('*>'): do_cmd_look (ui-knowledge.c:4169) calls target_set_interactive(TARGET_LOOK, -1, -1, true), and that last true is allow_pathfinding, so look mode is a targeting mode and handles '>', '<' and 'g' exactly as the manual says. I first wrote the opposite because 'l>' produced NO MESSAGE on a level with no known staircase - the failure path is bell() (ui-target.c:1506), and a bell draws no text in a text dump. The manual was right and this note was wrong: a silent screen is what a failed jump looks like, not a missing key. (2) Pressing '>' when NOT standing on a staircase prints 'I see no down staircase here.' and does NOT auto-navigate: do_cmd_go_down (cmd-cave.c:106) only falls through to do_cmd_navigate_down if the option autoexplore_commands is set, and it is OFF by default. (3) The targeting cursor IS drawn as a literal '*' in the map, so a plain-text player can SEE the cursor move - at ask 480 '*x' put the cursor on the tile 1 N of me. The 'x' key is path_nearest_unknown (nearest unexplored square); '>' is path_nearest_known(square_isdownstairs); both need the staircase to be KNOWN, so on a fresh level there is nothing for '>' to jump to. (ask 481)
- THE ESCAPE LADDER IS GONE. The pack at ask 492 holds exactly six items: a) Book of Nature Magics [Lesser Charms], b) 2 Rations, c) 23 Flasks of oil, d) 1 Potion of Cure Light Wounds, e) a Wooden Torch (3920 turns), f) a Cloak [1,+0]. There is NO Phase Door scroll and NO Word of Recall left - not stolen, SPENT: the prior life burned its Phase Door scrolls to escape (notebook ask 333) and read the Word of Recall to come home (ask 381, which also healed to full). The prior life's own REPORT says it ended with '22 flasks of oil, 1 Cure Light Wounds, 18 gold'. So the druid now has oil and a whip and nothing else: no scroll escape, no recall, no healing beyond one potion. What remains is: oil (46 lb of a ~108 lb budget), one CLW, and 3 gold with the shops out of reach. This changes the plan for this life - the run cannot leave the dungeon except by dying or by reaching a down staircase and going DEEPER, and a bad fight on depth 2-3 with no Phase Door is likely fatal. (ask 492)
- THE FASTEST EXPLORATION LOOP IN THE GAME, and it is in the manual only as a footnote: in TARGETING mode ('*') the digit keys move the CURSOR, not the player, and 'x' then 'g' will walk you to the nearest unexplored square to wherever the cursor is. Because the cursor is clamped to the level bounds (cave->width-2, cave->height-2) and 'x' is path_nearest_unknown(CURSOR), you can aim the cursor 40+ tiles into ground you have never seen and the pathfinder will then walk there THROUGH UNKNOWN TERRAIN, revealing it as it goes (find_path in player-path.c:1069 falls back from known-only to any-grid when the destination is unknown). Measured: '*~30 digits in one direction' + 'x' + 'g' walked 17 tiles and 170 turns on one ask (ask 520) and then 29 tiles and 290 turns on the next (ask 522). The digit keys move the cursor ONE tile per press, not the 10 that is_running_keymap() would give - the running-keymap test at ui-target.c:1617 did not fire for plain digits. So the recipe is: '*' then N repetitions of a digit direction, then 'x', then 'g'. The 'g' leaves targeting mode (ui-target.c:1488 sets done = true) so each ask is ONE walk. This is how a level of 198x66 can be covered at all: the plain '*xg' loop only advances the frontier by one tile per ask. (ask 522)
- THREE MORE THINGS MEASURED, and the first is the most useful command in the game for a plain-text player. (1) THE CURSOR-MOVE EXPLORATION LOOP: in targeting mode ('*') the digit keys move the CURSOR one tile per press, and 'x' then 'g' walks you to the nearest UNEXPLORED square to wherever the cursor is. But the far better version DROPS the 'x': '*' plus N repetitions of a direction digit, then 'g' alone, asks the game to pathfind to that exact grid, and find_path() (player-path.c:1069) falls back from a known-only path to one through unknown grids when the destination is unknown - so the walk goes THROUGH unexplored ground and reveals it. Measured walks this life: 170 turns (17 tiles), 290 turns (29 tiles), 310, 320, 330, 390 and 440 turns (22 tiles) on single asks, and the aim has to be BIG (30-70 tiles) or the destination lands in a wall and nothing happens at all. Two consecutive 'x'+'g' legs in one answer cancel each other: 'g' sets done=true and leaves targeting mode (ui-target.c:1488), and the next key then cancels the run - so one walk per ask is the real limit. (2) THE GREY MUSHROOM PATCH IS THE WORST MONSTER ON DEPTH 1: monster.txt gives it 2 hp, AC 1, NEVER_MOVE, blow SPORE:CONFUSE:1d4 - the 1d4 is the CONFUSION DURATION and it deals 1 damage a turn as well. Confusion is the single most crippling condition in the game: it blocks CASTING (player-util.c:1103 'You are too confused!'), blocks running and exploring (cmd-cave.c:1503), and randomises every direction you give - movement, attack and throw - with 75 percent probability (player_confuse_dir, player-util.c:1353), so you attack walls and throw oil at nothing. A Cure Light Wounds cures it for 20 turns and is worth more than its 20 healing when one is carrying. A melee whip at AC 1 kills the patch in one blow, and the whip's direction is randomised too, so twelve 'whip hits' in one answer make a hit very likely. Stinking Cloud hits it but the patch 'resists a lot' - every monster has IM_POIS. (3) THE ENTER KEY IS CARRIAGE RETURN, not newline: 'R50' followed by \n leaves the rest prompt sitting there with '50' in it and no turn passes; the same command with \r rests 500 turns. That cost me three asks. (ask 606)
- THE DEPTH 1 OF THIS SEED IS A DIFFERENT LEVEL FROM THE ONE THE PRIOR LIVES WALKED, and that is worth recording because it settles a question the notebook had left open. The prior life found a down staircase on depth 1 at ask 161 and descended; this life, after the Word of Recall sent it to town and back down at ask 437, found a DIFFERENT depth 1: the terrain is different (no '%' vein corridors at all, where the old level had them), the up staircase sits in a different place, and the game's own '>' jump to a KNOWN down staircase (path_nearest_known with square_isdownstairs, which requires square_isknown) finds nothing here - so the staircase the character descended is not merely unseen here, it is not remembered here either. The level was regenerated on the way back up. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANYBODY WHO CONTINUES THIS CHARACTER: the down staircase of depth 1 must be found again from scratch, and the only route that works is LOOKING at every glyph on every map, because the game's own tools ('>' for a known staircase, Magic Mapping, Detect Stairs) all require that the staircase already be known or the scroll be owned. OVER 174 SCREENS OF THIS LEVEL (the final count; the figure when the note was written was 171) I NEVER SAW A '>' GLYPH, and the level is 198x66 with exactly one down staircase placed uniformly at random over its floor (gen-cave.c:1583 allocates one; gen-util.c:620 places it on a square with three adjacent walls). THE SHAPE OF THE LEVEL I DID MAP, for whoever comes next: a long east-west corridor on one row running most of the width of the level, with the up staircase near its middle, rooms off it to the north and south, two LOCKED DOORS (one 1 north of the corridor near the up staircase, one 4 north and 4 east of it) whose rooms are entered only by picking the lock (Searching 26 percent, so expect three or four tries), several grey mushroom patches near the doors, and a large open chamber to the north-west reached by the corridor at its north end. The '>' is not in any of the rooms I entered. (ask 607)

- CORRECTION to the note at ask 481, made after this life ended and checked in the source: the '>' jump to a KNOWN down staircase works in LOOK mode ('l>') as well as in targeting mode ('*>'). do_cmd_look (ui-knowledge.c:4169) calls target_set_interactive(TARGET_LOOK, -1, -1, true) and that last true is allow_pathfinding, so look mode IS a targeting mode and handles '>', '<' and 'g' exactly as the manual says. What I saw at ask 475 was 'l>' producing no message on a level where no staircase was known - the failure path is bell() (ui-target.c:1506) and a bell draws no text in a text dump, so the cursor simply did not move. I turned a silent failure into a missing feature, and the manual was right. The general lesson, which is worth more than the fact: a key that produces no message and no turn may well have been handled and rejected; check the source before concluding the key does not exist. (corrected after the run)
- CARRIED ON from minimaxflash-1.3 at ask 609, turn 16981, replay identical=true, run minimaxflash-1.4. NOT read: any other run's decisions, report or notebook, PLAN.md, ACCUMULATED_KNOWLEDGE.md. (ask 609)
- PACK AT ask 610 (the inventory screen names four items, a-d): a Book of Nature Magics [Lesser Charms], b 2 Rations of Food, c 21 Flasks of oil (42.0 lb), d a Cloak [1,+0]. So life 3's Cure Light Wounds and Wooden Torch are GONE and two flasks of oil were spent since its ask-492 note. The druid now has NO healing potion, NO escape scroll and NO town ticket: the only things it owns are a whip, 21 flasks of oil and a spellbook. (ask 610)
- THE AIMED WALK, first measured this life: '*' then 40 x '8' (north) then 'g', no 'x'. The cursor clamps to the level bounds, so a 40-tile aim lands at the top edge; the path itself is computed by find_path (player-path.c:1107) where only_known = square_isknown(start) && square_isknown(dest), so an UNKNOWN destination makes unknown grids passable and the path crosses unexplored terrain. Whether that walk is long or a bogus short one is the disagreement between my own lives 2 and 3 (minimaxflash-2 said unknown destinations give a short meaningless path; minimaxflash-1.3 measured 17-29 tile walks with exactly this recipe). The turn counter on the next screen settles it. (ask 611)
- TWO ASKS LOST TO A MODAL SCREEN, and the rule is worth keeping: after 'i' or 'e' the game is still in a MENU and every key I send goes to the menu, not to the map. At ask 611 the '*' plus 40 eights plus 'g' were eaten by the equipment screen and produced a context menu ('Command for Soft Leather Armour'); the walk never happened and the map did not move. The escape is ESC twice: once out of the context menu, once out of the equipment screen. So after ANY screen that is not the map, send ESC before anything else. (ask 612)
- ESCAPE WORKS IN THE OBJECT CONTEXT MENU, and my ask 612 read as 'it does not' was wrong: the screen came back identical because the menu had cancelled, the equipment list was showing again, and my trailing 'g' - which is the letter of the Soft Leather Armour in that list - selected it and opened the context menu again. The tell is that the ESC worked and I undid it with the next key. RULE: never end an ask with a letter that names an item in a menu you are about to leave. (ask 613)
- THE ESCAPE TRAP, measured twice and costing four asks: in a key string the two-character escape '\e' is ONE Escape keypress, so '\ee' is Escape followed by the literal letter 'e'. To leave the object context menu AND the equipment list I need '\e\e'. My first two attempts sent '\ee' and the letter 'e' was consumed by the equipment list as a no-op, and the trailing 'g' then re-selected the Soft Leather Armour and reopened the context menu - so the screen looked identical and I wrongly concluded Escape did not work. (ask 614)
- THE AIMED WALK MEASURED, first good one this life: '*' + 40 x '6' (east) + 'g' with the cursor aimed at an UNKNOWN square did produce a path - it walked south out of the room, broke the open door at (7,13) and stopped at the grey mushroom patch at (7,14), which is a monster in the next square. So the path goes THROUGH unexplored ground as the source says (find_path, player-path.c:1107, only_known = square_isknown(start) && square_isknown(dest)), and the walk is stopped by a monster, a known trap or a disturbance. The message when it stops is 'Target Aborted.' (ask 615)
- THE SEALED ROOMS ARE THE BEST LEAD, and it comes from the generator plus my own life 3: alloc_stairs (gen-util.c:620) puts the down staircase on a square with exactly THREE adjacent walls - a dead end - and a room that is sealed behind a locked door is full of dead ends. Life 3 mapped this level for 174 screens and never saw a '>' because it never opened either locked door. So the two locked doors, not the open corridors, are where the staircase most likely is. (ask 616)
- A DIGIT STRING DOES NOT STOP AT A BLOCKED MOVE, and this corrects my own note from life 1 (which said it stops at the first wall and the rest is dropped). Twelve east presses from (7,13) into the wall at (8,13) moved me nowhere and printed no message, but the turn counter went up by about fourteen over that ask, so every blocked move cost a turn and the string kept going. So a string of repeats is a cheap way to hammer a locked door: each press is one pick attempt. (ask 617)
- THE SEALED-ROOM PLAN, step one: I am on the floor at (13,14) having come through the closed door at (8,14) (it opened on the first try, so it was closed, not locked). The passage runs north at cols 11-13 to a closed door at (13,10), and north of THAT door (13,9) is unexplored - the generator's three-walls rule makes a dead end a likely place for the one down staircase, and a room sealed behind a locked door is full of them. Repeated north presses cost one pick attempt each. (ask 618)
- A LOCKED DOOR STOPS A DIGIT STRING, and that is worth writing down because it is the opposite of what I assumed. Ten north presses moved me three tiles north and then stopped at the closed door at (13,10); the turn counter rose 80 over that ask, so the presses were consumed, but no message appeared and the door stayed '+'. Compare ask 617, where the string '266666666666' opened the closed door at (8,14) on the first press and carried on east for four more tiles: that door was CLOSED, this one is LOCKED. So a closed-but-unlocked door opens and the string continues; a locked door stops it, and each further press is one pick attempt. (ask 619)
- LOCK PICKING TAKES SEVEN TO TEN TURNS AND ONE PRESS EACH, and the message says 'You have picked the lock.' - that is the only message the locked door at (13,10) ever gave, which is why ten presses in one ask produced a silent screen and I read it as 'the string stopped'. It did not stop: the presses were spent picking, seven of them failed, and the eighth ask's single press worked. So a locked door does NOT stop a digit string, it just eats one press per attempt, and a long string of presses is the cheap way to pick a lock (26 percent a time). (ask 620)
- THE BIG ROOM IS A HUB, and this is the map of the level so far, which nobody else has: the big room at columns 16-29, rows 8-12 is walled on the east at column 30, so it is NOT a route to the eastern half. It has three ways out - west through the closed door at (14,8) where I stand, north up the one-tile corridor at column 19 to rows 3-2, and south down the corridor at column 17 to rows 14-19. The unexplored mass is east of column 30 and in rows 14-21, and the only way into the top strip is the column-19 corridor. So: open the door, go north, then run east along the top of the level. (ask 621)
- M SCALES THE WHOLE LEVEL, and this corrects three lives of my own notes. display_map (src/ui-map.c:761) computes row = (y * map_hgt) / cave->height and col = (x * map_wid) / cave->width for EVERY square of the level, so the M panel is a scaled picture of the entire 198x66 level, not a window into it. My notes said 'M is a window onto the level' and 'M shows only the remembered region'; the second half is right (map_info reads cave->memory, so unexplored squares are blank) but the first half is wrong - it is the whole level, scaled to 78x22. So M is the orientation tool I never had: it shows my absolute position on the level and the whole explored region at once. (ask 622)
- THE M MAP PUTS ME ON THE LEVEL, and this is the orientation nobody in this repository has: the '@' sits at panel column 56, row 15 of a 78x22 panel over a 198x66 level, so I am at LEVEL COLUMN 142, ROW 45, and the up staircase is at level (139,57). The whole explored region is a blob at level columns 96-160, rows 39-63 - life 3's 'long east-west corridor running most of the width' is a corridor of about 64 columns, not 198. So the unexplored level is: rows 0-39 (a band 198 wide, about 7700 squares), columns 0-96 in the south (2600 squares) and columns 160-198 (900 squares). The only route I can see into the north band is the one-tile corridor at level column 148, which is six tiles east of me. (ask 623)
- A FAILED LOCK PICK CANCELS THE REST OF THE KEY STRING, and that is the rule I needed: the message is 'You failed to pick the lock. Cancelled.' - Cancelled is the game's run-cancel message, so the remaining presses are eaten. A locked door therefore gets ONE pick attempt per ask, not one per press, and a digit string of repeats is useless against a lock. THE CHANCE IS IN THE SOURCE: calc_unlocking_chance (player-calcs.c:1676) returns MAX(2, skill - 4 * lock_power), the door's lock level is randint1(7) (gen-util.c:581) and a CL4 High-Elf Druid has SKILL_DISARM_PHYS = 30 + 10*3 + 4 = 64, so the chance is 36 to 60 percent - one attempt in two on average, not the 26 percent my notebook claimed. The skill is divided by ten if no_light(player), i.e. if the player's own square is dark. (ask 624)
- THE PLAN FOR THE REST OF THE BUDGET, with the M map as the instrument: I know my absolute position (level 142,45) and the shape of what is explored (a blob at level cols 96-160, rows 39-63). The unexplored level is rows 0-39 (a band 198 wide), cols 0-96 in the south, and cols 160-198. One down staircase, placed uniformly among the level's dead ends, so the only way to find it is coverage - and coverage of 13000 squares in 120 asks is not going to happen. So the sweep measures what it can: how much of the level one aimed walk covers, and where the staircase is NOT. The M map after every few asks is the honest way to count, and it is also the only view that shows the whole explored region at once, so it is where a missed '>' would show up. (ask 625)
- THE AIMED WALK IS SHORT WHEN THE DESTINATION IS UNKNOWN, and the reason is now clear from the source: find_path treats unknown grids as passable, so the path to a far unknown aim is a straight line through ground nobody has seen, and the walk stops at the first REAL wall. The walk I aimed 25 tiles north moved me two tiles and aborted. A digit string along KNOWN floor is the reliable way to cover distance, and 'lxg' (jump to the nearest unexplored square) is the reliable way to extend the frontier, because its destination is adjacent to ground already seen. So the sweep is a sequence of planned digit strings along known corridors, each ending by probing north into the dark. (ask 626)

IS AMBIGUOUS IN A TEXT DUMP. object.txt gives the oil kind graphics:!:y AND gives the potions graphics:!:d, and the only difference is the colour, which a plain-text player never sees. So a '!' on the floor may be a flask of oil or a potion, and the only way to tell is to look at it or to pick it up: what I picked up was 4 Potions of Cure Light Wounds, which is the potion the character has been without for two lives. The honest way to use it is to aim, look at the screen, and aim again - the cursor clamps to the level bounds, so a big aim is always a request for the edge of the level rather than a specific square, and the pathfinder is free to take whatever route it can find through ground that has never been seen. The character is now in the easternmost corridor anyone has reached on this level. (ask 658)
- THE AIMED WALK IS NOT A DIRECTION COMMAND, and that is the thing worth taking from three measurements: aiming 30 tiles east from the eastern corridor ended 27 tiles WEST, because the pathfinder takes whatever route reaches the destination and the direct one was walled off. So a big aim is a request for the edge of the level in that direction and the game decides how to get there - which is why it is good at covering ground and bad at going where you point. For a sweep that is exactly right: point west and let the game find the west. (ask 659)
- THE M MAP SHOWS THE SWEEP HAS STOPPED ADDING GROUND: the same footprint as ten asks ago, because the aimed walk takes routes the pathfinder knows about and those are the corridors I have already walked. The frontier walk is the other tool: in look mode the 'x' key jumps the cursor to the nearest square that is NOT remembered and 'g' walks there, so it always ends on new ground - and unlike the aimed walk it cannot be routed into a dead end three tiles away. This is the tool the earlier lives used 31 times and the tool that found a staircase in one ask in life two. (ask 660)
- WHETHER THE AIMED WALK FINDS NEW GROUND DEPENDS ON WHETHER THE DESTINATION IS KNOWN, and that resolves the disagreement between my own lives two and three. find_path sets only_known = square_isknown(start) && square_isknown(dest), so an aim that lands on a square I have already seen is pathed over remembered ground only and the walk is a stroll along corridors I have walked; an aim that lands on a square I have NOT seen is pathed through unknown ground, which the pathfinder treats as passable, and the walk crosses new territory as it goes. So the rule is: aim further than the edge of what you know. From level column 154 the known ground stops at 124, so a 45-tile aim lands 31 tiles into the dark. (ask 661)
- THE KEYPAD IS CONFIRMED FROM THE SOURCE and my slip was mine alone: ddx and ddy are indexed by the digit itself (cave.c: ddx = 0,-1,0,1,-1,0,1,-1,0,1 and ddy = 0,1,1,1,0,0,0,-1,-1,-1), so 4 is left, 6 is right, 8 is up, 2 is down, and target_dir_allow turns a digit into that index with D2I. So the aimed walk's direction is exactly what I ask for; what I do not control is the route. Two measurements in a row of the same recipe gave 33 tiles and 3 tiles, and both times the pathfinder went somewhere I did not point, because with an unknown destination it treats every unseen square as passable and the cheapest route to a point in the dark is not the straight one. (ask 662)
- THE AIMED WALK IS A LOTTERY AND THE DIGIT STRING IS NOT: aiming 45 tiles north moved me one tile south, because the path to the northern edge had to go through ground the pathfinder would not commit to. The reliable sweep is the digit string along a corridor to its end, then a door, then the next segment - and this level is nothing but corridors and doors. This is the tenth door and the pattern of the level is now clear: every door opens onto a two to four tile segment and another door, and the level is a lattice of them. (ask 663)
- THE EASTERN EDGE OF THE LEVEL IS REACHED: the corridor at row 14 runs to level column 192 of 198, which is the easternmost ground anyone has stood on in this character's four lives. Everything west of here is the lattice I have been walking, and the strip east of column 182 and the whole band north of row 21 are dark. (ask 664)
- SIX POINTS OF DAMAGE FROM NOTHING VISIBLE: the walk along row 14 cost 33 to 27 hit points with no monster on the map, and the status line still says no conditions - so it was an invisible floor trap (a dart trap does 2d6, and a trap is not drawn until it is detected). The character is then regenerating one point at a time, 27, 29, 30, which is the whole argument for the four Cure Light Wounds it picked up: on a level you sweep blind, the healing is not for the monsters. (ask 665)
- THE NORTHERN BAND'S ONLY VISIBLE GATEWAY IS A LOCKED DOOR FOUR TILES FROM ME, and the M map shows the whole band above it - level rows 0 to 20, all 198 columns, unexplored. Eight asks of aimed walking since the last M map moved me eleven tiles east and added no new ground at all, because the aimed walk keeps choosing routes over ground the pathfinder already knows; the digit string is what walks a corridor, and the doors are what reach new ground. So the sweep from here is: corridor, door, corridor, door. (ask 666)
- THE PANEL'S COLUMN SHIFT IS A TRAP FOR A READER, and I fell into it twice: the map's left edge is drawn behind the sidebar, so on a row whose sidebar text is one character short every glyph on that row is one column out. Two of my own maps disagreed with each other about where I was standing, and the only reliable position is the one on the M map, which is drawn on its own grid and not over a sidebar. So: the M map for where I am, look.py for what is next to me, and never a column number off a raw screen row. (ask 667)
- THE NORTHERN GATEWAY, at last: the closed door at (39,10) is one tile east, and beyond it the passage turns north along column 40 and then west to (39,9), which is the top row of the level and the start of the 21 unexplored rows above everything I have walked. Eleven locked doors on this level so far. (ask 668)
- THE DOOR AT (39,10) LED TO A NINE BY FOUR ROOM with a second closed door in its far wall at (43,12), and the room's north and south walls are solid, so every new piece of ground on this level arrives through a door and every door costs two asks. Twelve locked doors in one level is unusual and I would like to know from the generator whether that is normal for a 'classic' profile, because if it is normal then the down staircase is behind one of them and the sweep is the right plan. (ask 669)
- AN OPEN DOOR AT (39,7) IS FOUR NORTH AND FIVE WEST of me - on the level's top row - so the northern band does have doorways into it; the corridor I came along runs along the level's northern edge and comes in and out through these doors. That is the shape of the answer to my own lead: the north is reachable, but only through doors, and a door costs two asks and a walk. (ask 670)
- THE SWEEP FROM HERE IS A MATTER OF AIMING BIG AND LOOKING AT THE MAP: the cursor clamps to the level bounds, so any big aim is a request for the edge of the level in that direction, and the pathfinder takes the cheapest route it can find - a straight line where the ground is unknown, a detour where it is not. Eight different aims cover the eight directions of a level, and the M map after each one says what was actually gained. (ask 671)
- LOOK MODE IS THE NAVIGATOR I FORGOT I HAD: in look mode a direction key does not move the cursor one tile, it SNAPS it to the next interesting square in that direction - a door, a monster, an item, a staircase - and the message line then names it with its exact offset. So 'l' then a direction then 'g' is one ask to walk to the next door on the level, with the game doing the geometry and telling me what it found. That is worth more than the aimed walk, which spends an ask to go three tiles. (ask 672)
- THE NAVIGATOR THAT WORKS: 'l' then a direction then 'g' walked me five tiles north along a corridor to the next door in ONE ASK, and the game did the geometry. The aimed walk had been giving me one to three tiles for the same price, because it asks the pathfinder for a route to a distant square and the pathfinder does not know the way; the look-mode snap knows exactly where the next door is and the 'g' then follows the corridor to it. For a level that is nothing but corridors and doors this is the right tool, and it is in the manual only as a footnote. (ask 673)
- THE DOOR AT (39,6) WAS A DEAD END, and the map panel scrolling is what made it look otherwise: the panel shifts when the character nears its edge, so the same square appears at a different row on the next screen, and I spent two asks on a corridor that ended in a wall. The reliable reading is the M map for position and look.py for neighbours, and the reliable walking is 'l' plus a direction plus 'g'. (ask 674)
- TWELVE LOCKED DOORS AND NOT ONE STAIRCASE, and the level's shape is now certain: it is a lattice of long corridors with a locked door at the end of each arm, and the door opens onto a short segment and another door. The sweep has been through about 25 per cent of the level's squares and the M map has been checked after every ten asks, so there is no '>' glyph anywhere in the ground I have walked - which is the first time in this repository that the absence of the staircase has been checked against the whole explored region at once rather than against one panel at a time. (ask 675)
- GOLD DROPS ON DEPTH 1 ARE REAL, and the number is in the source: make_gold (obj-make.c:1296) averages (16 * lev) / 10 + 16 gold, so a monster at depth 1 drops about 17 gold when it drops any, with a spread of lev + 10. That is worth recording because the whole of this run's money problem was solved by three gold and a shop three hundred columns away - but it also says the way to buy a Magic Mapping scroll or a Phase Door is to kill things, and killing on depth 1 pays almost no experience at character level 4. (ask 676)
- FIVE DIRECTION AIMED WALKS FROM ONE SPOT, measured: north 1 tile, north-west 0, north 3, west 26 (the wrong way), south-west 1. The aimed walk is a slot machine - it asks the pathfinder for the level's edge and the pathfinder answers with whatever route it believes is cheapest, and an unknown destination makes unknown squares free, so the route tends to be a straight line that a real wall stops. The look-mode snap is the reliable one and the digit string is the cheap one; the aimed walk is for when I want to cross a lot of known ground in one ask. (ask 677)
- THE AIMED WALK KEEPS GOING EAST, and that is not me aiming badly: the destination was level column 107, in the dark western half, and the pathfinder's cheapest route to it runs east for 33 tiles first, which means the western corridors at this row are walled off from the pathfinder's point of view - it will not use a locked door it does not know how to open. So the aimed walk cannot reach the west and only the look-mode walk along known corridors can, one door at a time. (ask 678)
- THE LOOK-MODE WALK ALSO STOPS AT A WALL: 'l4g' from the top of this corridor did not move me because there is no interesting square west on the panel - the interesting squares are doors, monsters, items and staircases, and a wall is none of them. So the navigator and the aimed walk fail in the same place: a one-tile corridor whose walls stop every kind of jump. What works there is the digit string. (ask 679)
- THE KEYPAD, ONE LAST TIME, BECAUSE I GOT IT WRONG AGAIN: 8 is UP and 2 is DOWN. I sent five 8s meaning south and walked three tiles north. The digits are the only keys in this game that are not letters and they are the only ones I keep having to look up; the level of this level is that the game's own manual calls them 'digits walk' and never says which is which. (ask 680)
- THIRTEEN LOCKED DOORS, and the level's shape is now a certainty: corridors running east-west and north-south with a locked door at the end of each arm, and every door opens onto a short segment and another door. The down staircase is behind one of them, and this level has a great many of them. (ask 681)
- THE CORRIDOR AT ROW 14 RUNS EAST OFF THE EDGE OF THE PANEL, and that is the first time in this sweep that a corridor has left the visible panel rather than ending at it. The map window is 66 columns wide and the level is 198, so a corridor that leaves the panel is a corridor into unmapped level. (ask 682)
- NEW GROUND AT LAST, and the look-mode walk is what found it: a ten-digit string east walked the panel across the level and revealed a whole new set of corridors and three doors I had not seen, at (42,7), (45,12) and (48,21). The panel scrolling under the character makes two screens look like a teleport when they are a walk, which is why the M map is the only honest position. (ask 683)
- THE LOOK-MODE WALK IS ONE ASK AND SEVERAL TILES, and it works through a level that is all corridors: 'l' then a direction snaps the cursor to the next door, monster, item or staircase in that direction and 'g' walks the corridor to it. Six tiles north in one ask here. On a level whose rooms are all behind locked doors this is the cheapest way to cover ground there is. (ask 684)
- THE CORRIDOR AT COLUMN 42 REACHES ROW 2, and the level's northern band - the 14 rows above everything I have walked - begins right there. The whole sweep has been climbing north one locked door at a time, and this is the corridor that gets above the last door. (ask 685)
- THE NORTH EDGE OF THE LEVEL, and it is a corridor: a one-tile passage at column 46 running from row 11 up to row 0, which is the northern boundary of the dungeon. Six of my last eight asks were climbing to it. This is the northern band at last - the fourteen rows above everything the earlier lives walked - and the staircases of a 'classic' level sit in rooms, so there should be rooms off this corridor. (ask 686)
- A FIFTEEN BY SEVEN ROOM AT THE LEVEL'S NORTH EDGE, rows 4 to 10, columns 39 to 53, with an unidentified scroll lying in it. That room is the northern band: eleven rows that no life of this character has ever seen, entered at last through thirteen locked doors and a corridor that runs to the dungeon wall. (ask 687)
- A SCROLL OF LIGHT IS WORTH MORE ON A SWEEP THAN IT LOOKS: the character's torch shows two tiles, so every step memorises about four squares of the level, and a permanent light globe would memorise a whole room in one turn. The two scrolls on the floor had the same title and turned out to be different kinds - one Blessing, one Light - so an unidentified object's title is not its kind, and the only way to know is to read it. A Scroll of Light costs nothing but a turn, and it makes the last hundred asks of this sweep cover much more ground. (ask 688)
- THE SCROLL OF LIGHT LIFTS THE LIGHT LEVEL FROM 2 TO 3 and shows the whole northern room at once: rows 3 to 11, columns 39 to 57, which is nineteen by nine squares of the level that no life of this character has seen. It is a dead end - one corridor in at column 46 and no door - which is a useful thing to know about the north band: the rooms there are sealed, and the staircases in a classic level sit in exactly that kind of room. (ask 689)
- THE NORTHERN ROOM IS A DEAD END - nineteen by nine squares, no door, one corridor in - and it holds no staircase. So the level's north band is a row of sealed rooms and the staircase is not in them. The western half of the level, columns 0 to 124, is still dark and it is two thirds of the dungeon; the aimed walk is the only thing that can cross that much ground, if the pathfinder will go west, and so far it has refused three times and sent me east instead. (ask 690)
- THE AIMED WALK GOES WEST WHEN THERE IS A WAY WEST: from the northern room the pathfinder found a route and covered 24 tiles into ground nobody had seen, and the level's up staircase turned up five tiles north - so the region I had been circling for twenty asks was next to the place I started the sweep from. The western half is still open and the walk is finding it now that the north band has been crossed. (ask 691)
- THERE IS MORE THAN ONE UP STAIRCASE ON THIS LEVEL - I have now met two - and exactly one down staircase, and the generator keeps them at least sixteen tiles apart. That is worth recording because it kills a hope: an up staircase is not a way down, and the number of up staircases on a level says nothing about where the down one is. (ask 692)
- THE AIMED WALK IS A SLOT MACHINE AND THE PRIZE IS THE UNEXPLORED NORTH: the up staircase at (52,3) is three tiles north and two up, and the level's northern rooms are sealed, so the down staircase has to be in a corridor end or a room I have not entered - and there are fifteen rows of them above the band I crossed. (ask 693)
- TWO OF THE FIVE WESTWARD AIMS HAVE GONE WEST AND COVERED 24 TILES OF NEW GROUND, and the western two thirds of the level is the only part of it that is still worth sweeping: the east is walked, the north band is walked, and the level is 198 columns wide with my westernmost reach at about column 124. (ask 694)
- A LOCKED DOOR IN THE WESTERN DIRECTION, one tile away, and it is the fourteenth on this level. The sweep has become simply: find a door, open it, walk the corridor behind it, find the next door. Every door costs two asks and every corridor one, and the level's western two thirds have not been touched. (ask 695)
- THE KEYPAD, THIRD TIME IN THIS RUN, AND I WILL WRITE IT ON MY HAND: 4 IS WEST, 6 IS EAST, 8 IS NORTH, 2 IS SOUTH. I sent two 6s meaning west and walked east. What makes this costly is that the error is invisible - the character moves, the turn counter moves, and the map looks reasonable - so it takes the M map to notice that a walk went the wrong way. (ask 696)
- FIFTEEN LOCKED DOORS OPENED, and the pattern of the level is a corridor lattice with a locked door at every third segment: the generator makes ordinary dungeon doors LOCKED as often as not, which is why this level has fifteen of them, and it is why the earlier lives' 'the staircase must be behind a locked door' hunch never paid off - the doors are not rare enough to be a sign. (ask 697)
- TWO CLOSED DOORS NORTH AND SOUTH OF THE SAME SPOT, and a corridor north that no life of this character has walked. The level is more doors than floor: fifteen locked doors in about two hundred tiles of corridor, every third segment, and the staircase has to be at the end of one of them. (ask 698)
- A FOURTEEN BY FIVE ROOM AT THE LEVEL'S NORTH-WEST, with a door in its north wall at (48,2) and a corridor south. The level's north rooms are all big and all sealed, and every one of them has been empty of staircases so far. (ask 699)
- THE NORTHERN ROOMS ARE ALL EMPTY AND ALL SEALED - three of them now - so the down staircase is not in a room on this level. It is at the end of a corridor, and the corridors are the only thing left to sweep. (ask 700)
- THE NORTH-WEST CORNER OF THE LEVEL: a corridor at column 42 running up to row 0, which is the dungeon's northern wall. The level is 198 columns wide and this is around column 130 of them, so the western half is still a hundred columns of corridor lattice away. (ask 701)
- THE NORTH-WEST CORNER ROOM OF THE LEVEL, ten by four, at rows 2 to 5 - and the room's west side runs off the edge of what is remembered. The north-west corner is the last piece of the level I can reach from here, and beyond it is the hundred columns of corridor lattice that makes up the western half. (ask 702)
- THE NORTH-WEST CORNER, and the level's northern edge is the one place where a corridor might run for a hundred columns: the room's west side is open at row 4. If the edge of the level has a passage along it, the whole western half becomes one long walk, and that is the last hope for the staircase in this life. (ask 703)
- THE NORTHERN EDGE OF THE LEVEL IS A CORRIDOR, and it runs west: eleven tiles in one ask, with an icky thing in the passage which the string will fight on the way through. A one-wide corridor along the top of a 198-wide level is the cheapest possible route into ground nobody has walked, and this is the last hope for the staircase in this life. (ask 704)
- THE ICKY THING DIED IN FOUR SWINGS (six hit points, to-hit 19 against armour class 7, and eight attacks cost one ask) and the corridor along the level's northern edge goes on west. This is the first time in this sweep that a straight walk has carried me into unknown ground for more than a dozen tiles. (ask 705)
- TWELVE TILES WEST ALONG THE LEVEL'S NORTHERN EDGE, and the corridor is still going: the panel now starts at level column 5 and the corridor runs to column 46, so this passage is a quarter of the level's width and it is the first long unbroken stretch of the dungeon anyone has walked. (ask 706)
- THE WESTERN EDGE OF THE LEVEL, and the whole of the north side is now one long corridor from edge to edge: the panel's row 4 runs unbroken for forty columns with only vein walls above and below it. South of me is the last unexplored region, the western half of the level, and it is where the staircase has to be. (ask 707)
- THE NORTHERN CORRIDOR IS SEALED SOUTH BY VEIN WALLS, which is why it is a dead end for the sweep and why the down staircase - which the generator puts on a square with exactly three adjacent walls - could be anywhere along it. This corridor runs the width of the level's north edge and no life of this character has walked more than a few columns of it. (ask 708)
- TEN MORE TILES WEST, and the corridor is still going with no doors in it at all - a plain passage along the edge of the dungeon, walled by vein above and below. If the down staircase is at the end of a passage like this one, then it is at the west end of the level's northern corridor, and I am walking towards it. (ask 709)
- THE WEST END OF THE NORTHERN CORRIDOR IS A TWO BY THREE POCKET at columns 18 and 19, and above it is unexplored: the corridor does not simply stop, it widens. The staircase wants a square with three walls, and a pocket like this is exactly where a generator would put one. (ask 710)
- THE CORRIDOR ALONG THE LEVEL'S NORTHERN EDGE ENDS IN A TWO BY TWO POCKET with no staircase in it, and the corridor has now been walked from one end to the other - which makes it the longest single stretch of this level that any life has seen, and it held nothing but wall. (ask 711)
- THE M MAP SAYS THE SWEEP HAS COVERED ABOUT HALF THE LEVEL: level columns 81 to 178, rows 0 to 63, which is 97 by 66 squares of the 198 by 66 level, and there is still no '>' glyph in any of it. The last dark region is the western fifth of the level, columns 0 to 81, and the northern corridor runs straight into it. (ask 712)
- THE NORTHERN CORRIDOR ENDS AT LEVEL COLUMN 81 and the western fifth is not reachable from it. The last route into the west is through the middle of the level, so the aimed walk asks for the level's south-west corner and the pathfinder has to find its own way through the lattice. (ask 713)
- THE PATHFINDER KEEPS PREFERRING EAST: aimed at the level's south-west corner it delivered me 32 tiles east along the northern corridor, because from here that is the only route it knows. Three aims west in a row have gone west twice and east once, and the two that went west covered 24 tiles of new ground each. (ask 714)
- THE REMAINING DARK HALF OF THE LEVEL IS IN ITS SOUTH-WEST QUARTER, and the only route to it that the pathfinder can be given is south: the level's southern rows are unexplored from the eastern blob westward, and the level's southern edge is as good a destination as any. (ask 715)
- THE NORTHERN CORRIDOR IS SEALED FROM THE LEVEL BELOW BY VEIN WALLS except at its eastern end, so the western fifth of the level can only be entered from the south. The aimed walk has to be given the south-west corner and hope the pathfinder finds a way down and round. (ask 716)
- THE WESTERN FIFTH OF THE LEVEL IS ENTERED FROM THE SOUTH: the level's southern rows from column 0 to 96 are unexplored and the eastern blob's southern edge is at column 96, so walking west along the level's southern rows is the last route into it. The northern corridor is a dead end at column 81 and the middle of the level is where I have to go back to. (ask 717)
- THE PACK AT ASK 718, for the record: a Book of Nature Magics [Lesser Charms], 2 Rations of Food, 20 Flasks of oil, 4 Potions of Cure Light Wounds, 2 Scrolls (one of them a Scroll of Blessing already read, one of them a Scroll of Light already read) and a Cloak [1,+0]; the Wooden Torch is the light source and is not in the pack. So the character that three lives ago had no potion, no escape and no way home now has four heals, twenty flasks and a permanent light - and still no down staircase. (ask 718)
- NXT WENT FROM 28 TO 26, so the sweep has earned two experience units after all - the icky thing, the centipede and the snake between them - which at character level 4 on depth 1 is what the game's own formula (monster experience x monster level / player level) allows. Two units in a hundred asks is the whole argument about this level: at depth 1 and level 4 a kill is worth a quarter of an experience unit, so a character that wants to level must go DEEPER, and going deeper needs the one staircase this level is hiding. (ask 719)
- THE COVERAGE IS NOW MEASURABLE: level columns 76 to 185 and rows 0 to 63, which is 109 by 66 squares of a 198 by 66 level - 55 per cent - with no '>' glyph anywhere in it. The remaining 45 per cent is the western 78 columns, and the northern corridor's west end at column 78 is a dead end two tiles from it. (ask 720)
- THE SOUTH-WEST CORNER IS UNREACHABLE FROM HERE even by the pathfinder, which treats unknown ground as passable - so the western 78 columns are sealed off from the northern corridor by more than the corridor's end. The route to them has to be through the southern rows, and that means going back east first. (ask 721)
- THE PATHFINDER IS NOT A COMPASS: aimed east it delivered 33 tiles west, because it answers with the cheapest route it can find and the cheapest route from the pocket at the corridor's west end is along the corridor itself. The aimed walk is for covering ground, not for going where you point - the direction only tells it which edge of the level to aim for. (ask 722)
- THE WESTERN FIFTH IS 78 COLUMNS AND A FEW THOUSAND DEAD ENDS, and the last of the budget is going on it. If it is not there, the honest result of this life is a level mapped to 55 per cent and a staircase that is not in the mapped part. (ask 723)
- THE SOUTHERN ROWS ARE THE LAST REACHABLE DARK: level columns 0 to 96 at rows 39 to 63 are unexplored and the eastern blob's southern edge is at column 96, so a walk west along the level's southern rows would cover the western fifth. The path to them goes along the northern corridor and then down, which is what an aim at the level's southern edge asks the pathfinder for. (ask 724)
- THE LAST OF THE SWEEP. The character has 32 decisions left and the staircase is in the western 45 per cent of a level it has mapped to 55 per cent; the honest thing is to spend a few more asks on the one route that reaches it - the southern rows - and then to write down what was measured, because the measurement is what this life is worth. (ask 725)
- THIRTY-THREE TILES WEST puts the character at the western end of the level's northern corridor, and the aimed walk has now been measured at 0, 1, 3, 24, 26, 32 and 33 tiles on the same recipe - which is the number worth putting in the report: the aimed walk covers an average of about seventeen tiles an ask and its direction is not under the player's control. (ask 726)
- THE LAST AIMED WALKS. After this the run stops and the report is written, because a run that spends its last asks on a lottery and has nothing to say is worth less than one that says exactly what it measured. (ask 727)
- THE WESTERN END OF THE LEVEL, level column about ten, in the northern corridor. The character has walked this corridor from one end to the other three times over the sweep, which is the clearest single measurement of the run: a level's north edge is a 198-column passage with vein walls above and below it and nothing in it at all. (ask 728)
- THE COVERAGE IS 57 PER CENT OF THE LEVEL (level columns 73 to 185, rows 0 to 63) with no '>' glyph in it, and the character stands at the western end of the northern corridor with the level's western 73 columns dark in front of it. If the level has a corridor along its western edge, as it has along its northern edge, then this is the way into the last third. (ask 729)
- THE WESTERN REGION OPENS WITH A CHEST, and this is the first thing in four lives that could change the run: a chest on depth 1 is filled from the depth-1 object table, and that table includes the Deep Descent scroll (alloc 20:1 to 100 - about 7 per cent of depth-1 scrolls), gold (about 17 a drop), potions and staves. The west of this level is a different district of it - different corridors, a chest, an up staircase of its own at (30,8) - and it is exactly the ground the earlier lives never walked. (ask 730)
- THE CHEST IS AN EMPTY ONE: 'You see nothing there to open' means its pval is 0, which is the same empty chest the first life of this character found and could not open. A chest on depth 1 is filled from the depth-1 object table, so an empty one is a small thing - but the western district is not: a corridor twenty-two tiles long, a closed door, a monster and an up staircase of its own at (30,8). (ask 731)
- THE WESTERN DISTRICT HAS ITS OWN CORRIDOR LATTICE - a twenty-three tile passage at row 3 with a bat in it, a chest at its west end, a closed door, and passages at rows 4 to 9 that are cut off from each other - and none of it has a down staircase in it. The bat bit me for one and I am at full health; a fruit bat is 1d1 and worth three quarters of an experience unit at level 4. (ask 732)
- A FRUIT BAT IN A ONE-WIDE CORRIDOR IS A WALL, and the game has no way past it: eight swings of the whip at to-hit 19 against its armour class is about 87 per cent a hit, and it has four hit points, so one ask of eight attacks kills it and the rest of the string walks on. This is the cheapest fight in the game and it is the same fight as the mushroom patch in life three, where the whip was the answer and the oil was never needed. (ask 733)
- THE BAT IS DEAD AND THE CORRIDOR RUNS ON, and the western district's row 3 passage is twenty-two tiles with a chest at one end and a wall at the other. The level is a lattice of such passages and the down staircase is at the end of one of them, and I have walked about thirty of them without finding it. (ask 734)
- THE LAST AIMED WALK WEST. If it does not reach the level's western edge the sweep ends here, with the level mapped to more than half its squares, fifteen locked doors opened, three corridors of the north edge walked end to end, and no down staircase anywhere in what was walked. (ask 735)
- THE WESTERN DISTRICT HAS CORRIDORS AT ROWS 4 TO 9 THAT I HAVE NOT WALKED, and the level's southern edge is the only place the western third can be entered from. Twenty asks are left and they are for the staircase. (ask 736)
- THE GIANT WHITE CENTIPEDE BLOCKS THE ONLY WAY SOUTH: nine hit points, armour class 12, and the whip's to-hit of 19 against 12 is about 60 per cent, so four or five swings kill it and the rest of the string carries on south into the rows 4 to 9 corridors of this district. (ask 737)
- THE WESTERN DISTRICT HAS ITS OWN UP STAIRCASE six tiles east of me, which means the level has at least three of them, and it has its own lower lattice at rows 4 to 9 with a door at (26,4) that I never opened. The south-west corner of the level is the last thing the aimed walk has not been asked for from here. (ask 738)
- ANOTHER DISTRICT, another chest at (55,2) and another up staircase at (63,8), and the level is turning out to be a dozen of these little neighbourhoods rather than one blob. The character is at level column 40 now, in a place no life of it has been, and the last asks are for the chest and for the level's south-west corner. (ask 739)
- THE SECOND CHEST OF THE RUN, and it is the first one worth opening: a chest on depth 1 is filled from the depth-1 object table, and that table has a Deep Descent scroll in it at about 7 per cent. Fifteen asks are left, so whatever is in this chest is the last thing this life gets to do with. (ask 740)
- EVERY CHEST ON THIS LEVEL IS AN EMPTY ONE - two checked now, and a third in the first life of this character - and the message is the same each time: 'You see nothing there to open', which is what a chest with pval 0 says. So a depth-1 chest of this level is not a treasure and a player should not spend asks on them; that is one thing this life settled that three lives of chests did not. (ask 741)
- THE LAST OF THE PACK IS SPENT: the Scroll of Blessing is read for its five points of armour class and ten of to-hit, and the character ends this life at armour class 17 with a whip that can reach armour class 36 - which is the first time in four lives that this druid has been able to hurt anything with its own hands. (ask 742)
- TWO ASKS LEFT AFTER THIS ONE AND THE MAP, and then the run stops and the report is written. (ask 743)
- BLESSED, AND IT SHOWS IN THE FIGHT: the whip's to-hit is 29 against the centipede's armour class of 12, about 68 per cent a hit against the 60 per cent it was before, so the same fight takes three swings instead of five. That is the whole argument for spending a scroll on a buff rather than on an escape in a level this shallow. (ask 744)
- THE CENTIPEDE DIED IN THREE SWINGS once blessed, and the corridor west of it is open. This is the last aimed walk; the next screen is the final map and then the run is written up. (ask 745)
- THE LAST TWO WALKS OF THE RUN, then the map, then the write-up. (ask 746)
- THE PRAYER EXPIRED, which is how the game says the Blessing is over - thirty turns of plus five armour class and plus ten to-hit for one scroll and about a minute of play. That is the real price of a buff: on this level it did not last long enough to matter. (ask 747)

note: THROW MISSED the sleeping ant at distance 2 (ask 201: 'The giant black ant is targeted... The Flask of oil breaks' with NO damage line, and ask 205 confirms the ant is still 'unhurt, asleep'). Source reading (vendor/angband/src/player-attack.c): make_ranged_throw() applies the OF_EXPLODE x3 damage ONLY if test_hit() passed - a miss breaks the flask on the floor and does nothing. The hit chance is chance_of_missile_hit_base() minus distance, against the monster's AC. The ant's AC 24 (monster.txt) is brutal: hit_chance() needs to_hit >= ac*2/3 = 16 to have any chance above the flat 12% always-hit, so at range you are mostly rolling the 12%. (ask 205)
